message: Comparator is explicit (pooled ridge, lags 1-4 + 4/13-week rolling means, alpha=1.0, raw-demand control) and the treatment arm is exactly one change (log1p target, naive inverse), so the contrast is clean and the exclusion list (no yoy/promo/trend/cat/clip/window/series_mean) removes obvious confounds. Statement and estimand match: relative WAPE reduction on next-4-week unit-sum, evaluated on the raw scale for both arms via the naive back-transform, assessed by two-way (series x origin) bootstrap. kills_if is concrete and pre-specifies the CI-lower-bound rule, and correctly folds null/negative point estimates into the kill condition. Design B's origin count (32) vs A/C is justified on variance-stability grounds for resolving a 1% SESOI at alpha=0.025, and that tradeoff isn't something I'm second-guessing. No leakage: lag/rolling-mean features are computed from history at/before the origin week and the target is the forward 4-week sum, so features are known at forecast time under the stated setup. No blocking issues. One non-blocking note: since the naive log-transform is expected to underpredict via Jensen's-gap shrinkage, consider whether the bootstrap CI reporting also surfaces the raw point estimate/direction so a systematic-underprediction failure mode is visible to the team even on a kill, not just the CI bound.
new_hypothesis_for_pi: As already flagged in the rationale: preregister a separate hypothesis testing a bias-corrected log-transform (e.g., smearing estimator or exp(pred + sigma^2/2) correction) against the same raw-demand comparator, independent of whether logdem-v1 (naive, uncorrected) is killed.
